pages.title: Talking About Your Hobbies

situation.text: You sit on a park bench next to a stranger. You start a friendly chat and talk about what you like to do in your free time.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can start a small talk in a park, say what you like to do, ask about hobbies and suggest doing something together.
canDo: Ask: What do you do in your free time?
Say what you like: I like to… / I’m into…
Say how often you do it
Invite someone to try your hobby
success: I say what I like to do.
pages.think: What do people ask when they want to know you better? Do you ask about hobbies in Portuguese?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra que associa à situação de hoje.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
extra: What hobby would you like to try?
What is your friend’s hobby?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: Unit 6 and earlier: “I usually…” for routines. Ask: What do you usually do after work or school?

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Americans often use hobbies as small talk. It is an easy and safe topic with new people. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Many public libraries have reading groups and craft classes.
Photo walks and camera clubs are a popular way to meet people.
Many towns have community leagues for adults.

qs.q: What is a good small-talk question with a new person?
qs.pt: Qual é uma boa pergunta para puxar conversa?

levels.A1: What do you do for fun?
levels.A2: You can ask: What do you do in your free time?
levels.B1: Asking about hobbies is friendly and not too personal.
levels.B2: Hobbies are a safe topic: they open the conversation without being too personal.

qs.pt: Por que as pessoas entram em clubes?

levels.A2: They join clubs to learn something and meet new friends.
levels.B1: Clubs give people a regular activity and a group of friends who share an interest.
levels.B2: Clubs create a social routine around a shared interest, which makes it easier to build friendships as an adult.

qs.q: What happens after “I like to paint”?
qs.pt: O que acontece depois de “I like to paint”?

levels.A2: The other person usually asks a follow-up: Really? What do you paint?
levels.B1: A follow-up question shows interest and keeps the conversation going.
levels.B2: Native speakers rarely stop at one answer: they add a detail and return the question.

pages.compare: In Brazil people often talk about football, work or family first. In the USA, “What do you do for fun?” is also a very common opener. What is the first question you ask a new friend?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: What do you do in your free time?
Q2: para conhecer pessoas e aprender algo.
Q3: And you? / Really? What do you…?
extra: Do you prefer hobbies alone or with people?
What do you do on rainy days?

stretch: B2: compare as convenções sociais do Brasil e dos EUA nessa situação.

pass1.pt: Sobre o que eles estão conversando?

Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In English the important words are strong and the small words are weak: “I LIKE to PAINT”. This gives the sentence its natural rhythm.

items.say: What do you do in your free time?
items.linked: What do you DO in your FREE TIME?

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — meet someone in the park

brief.teacher: You are a friendly person on the next bench (change the plan during the scene!).
brief.student: You are new in the park: talk about your real hobbies and invite the other person.

orders: Talk about a sport you like
Talk about music or movies you like
Talk about something you do at home
complications: The other person has the same hobby: ask for details.
The other person doesn’t know the hobby: explain it simply.
You can’t go on the day they suggest: propose another day.
You didn’t understand: ask them to repeat.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a new friend from the park. Say what you like to do and invite them.
pages.model: Hi Paul! It was nice to meet you. **I like to paint** and **I’m into** watercolors. I paint **every Sunday** in the park. **Do you want to** come this Sunday? See you!
checklist: I said what I like to do.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Name a hobby with short phrases.

ladder.say: I’m into painting. I paint every Sunday. Do you want to come?
I took up painting last year, and it really helps me relax after work.
What I enjoy most is that it lets me switch off completely, whatever kind of week I’ve had.
I’d say it’s less a hobby than a way of keeping myself sane.
ladder.goal: Use nuance and a personal view.

ladder.say: For me it has quietly become the thread that holds the week together.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
